reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In a game, Mysong and Naoki are making problems. They each have four cards like these.

[1] [2] [3] [4]

The winner of the game is the person who can make the problem with the largest answer.

Mysong placed the cards like this.

[Image: Mysong's card placement]

Naoki placed the cards like this.

[Image: Naoki's card placement]

Who won this game? ____
How do you know? ____
____

descriptors: Mysong. 64 and 55 are shown (or 9, which is the difference between 64 and 55) with a correct verbal explanation.
Mysong. 64 and 55 are shown (or 43 − 31 > 24 − 21) with an unsatisfactory explanation.
Mysong. 64 and 55 are shown (or 43 − 31 > 24 − 21) without any further explanation.
Mysong. The response given is a verbal explanation. Either 64 or 55 is shown but not both.
Mysong. The response gives no verbal or numeric explanation.
Other responses containing Mysong. For example, “because Mysong had the largest answer.”
Neither Mysong nor Naoki win.
Naoki. There may or may not be an explanation.
Other incorrect, including “both won.”

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

A.

USE: 1 Triangle Tile and
1 Trapezoid Tile
MAKE: A 4-sided figure
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors:
Correct 4-sided figure turned in any position
[Image: A parallelogram composed of one trapezoid tile and one triangle tile]
Makes a larger triangle
Makes a 4-sided figure, but not using the specified tiles, e.g., a larger parallelogram.
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part A response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
